newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares pushed down by Salus.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares pushed down by Salus.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.09 percent on Tuesday, knocked down by a more than eight percent fall in pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus, traders said.
Salus, which was the day's leading decliner, lost 8.67 percent to 12,330 tolars on volume of 200 shares due to the prolonged court case concerning the company's privatisation in 1990, they added.
The SBI index dropped 14.42 points to 1,306.46.

Market participants said shares were likely to fall further in the next two weeks as many small shareholders of newly privatised companies were expected to sell shares ahead of holidays starting on May 1.

"Many first time shareholders of newly privatised firms may decide to sell their shares before the May holidays, being tired of waiting for prices to return to the high February levels -- which is unlikely to happen any time soon," said Nina Jarc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska Banka.

Since February 11, when the Bank of Slovenia blocked foreign trading by saying international investors have to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in securities, the SBI index has dropped 21.1 percent.
Overall 11 shares fell, two rose, one was unchanged and 13 were untraded. Turnover rose to 54.5 million tolars from 46.2 million.

Issue A of drug maker Lek was the most actively traded, falling 0.8 percent to 24,780 tolars on volume of 428 shares. Traders said Lek could ease to 22,000 tolars in the next two weeks if small shareholders decide to sell.
Shopping centre operator BTC was the top gainer, up 0.7 percent to 13,000 tolars on volume of 52 shares.
